## Purpose

This procedure describes the collection, handling, and field
documentation of sediment samples from streams, rivers, lakes, and
reservoirs. Sediment is a major sink and source of nutrients, metals,
organic contaminants, and fine particles in aquatic systems. The
procedures in this SOP are designed to produce samples suitable for
physical characterization (grain size, organic matter content),
chemical analysis (metals, nutrients, organic contaminants), and
biological assessment (benthic invertebrate habitat substrate)
[@mudroch1999; @usepa2001sediment].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Surficial sediment sampling (top 0--10 cm) in
  wadeable streams, non-wadeable rivers (from bridges or boats), and
  lentic systems (lakes, ponds, reservoirs). Deeper cores for
  stratigraphic or paleolimnological work follow the same safety and
  documentation requirements but use specialized coring equipment
  not covered in detail here.
- **Does not apply to:** Soil sampling on upland or riparian surfaces
  (see [SOP-F400](SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd)); suspended sediment
  sampling by filtration (see future SOP-L312); bedload transport
  measurements; marine sediment sampling
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve sampling plan, coordinate permits   |
| Trained Personnel | Collect and handle samples per this SOP     |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent sampling |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Wading in streams and working from boats carry slip,
  fall, and drowning hazards. Sediment sampling often involves
  bending, lifting, and handling heavy wet material.
- **Biological:** Sediment may harbor pathogens, parasites (e.g.,
  *Schistosoma*, *Naegleria*), and sharp debris (glass, metal).
- **Chemical:** Sediment from urban or industrial sites may contain
  heavy metals, hydrocarbons, or pesticides. Avoid skin contact
  and do not ingest.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (doubled for contaminated sites)
- [ ] Wading boots or hip waders
- [ ] Personal flotation device (boat sampling)
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Sun protection

### Emergency Procedures

A minimum of two people must be present for any in-water work. Refer
to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

### Sampling Devices

| Device                     | Application                                 | Notes                          |
|:---------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Stainless steel scoop or trowel | Wadeable stream surficial sediment    | Simplest; suitable for coarse to fine sediment |
| Ponar grab sampler (standard or petite) | Lakes, deep pools, non-wadeable rivers | Collects approximately 0.023 m^2^ (petite) to 0.052 m^2^ (standard) |
| Ekman grab sampler         | Soft lake-bottom sediment (silt, clay, organic muck) | Lighter than Ponar; not suitable for sand or gravel |
| Hand corer (acrylic tube, 5--7 cm ID) | Intact surficial cores in soft sediment | Preserves vertical stratigraphy |
| Gravity corer or piston corer | Deep cores for paleolimnological work | Specialized; consult PI       |

### Support Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Stainless steel bowls and spoons      | For homogenizing grab samples  |
| Pre-labeled sample bags (Whirl-Pak) or jars | Appropriate to analyte (see Section 7) |
| Cooler with ice packs                 | Maintain samples at 4 C        |
| Deionized water (squeeze bottle)      | For rinsing equipment          |
| Measuring tape and depth rod          | For recording water depth at sample location |
| GPS unit                              | For recording coordinates per [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd) |
| Field notebook and data sheets        | Waterproof (Rite in the Rain)  |
| Camera                                | For photo-documenting sample location and sediment appearance |
| Chain of custody forms                | Per [SOP-F008](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd) |


## Procedure

### Site Selection and Documentation

1. Identify the sampling location based on the study design (e.g.,
   depositional zones for contaminant assessment, riffles for
   substrate characterization)
2. Record GPS coordinates, date, time, water depth, and a visual
   description of the sediment surface (color, texture, odor,
   presence of debris or biota) in the field notebook
3. Photograph the site and the sediment surface before disturbing it

### Stream Sediment (Wadeable)

1. Approach the sampling location from downstream to avoid disturbing
   the target area
2. Using a stainless steel scoop or trowel, carefully skim the top
   5--10 cm of sediment. Avoid collecting underlying undisturbed
   substrate unless the study requires a depth profile.
3. Transfer the sediment into a stainless steel bowl
4. If a composite sample is required, collect sediment from 3--5
   locations within the reach (e.g., across the channel width at the
   designated transect) and combine in the bowl
5. Homogenize using a stainless steel spoon; remove large rocks,
   sticks, and debris
6. Transfer the homogenized sample into the appropriate container(s)
   (see Section 7)

### Lake and Reservoir Sediment (Grab Sampler)

1. Lower the Ponar or Ekman grab sampler to the bottom on a measured
   line from a boat or dock. Record the water depth.
2. Trip the sampler per the manufacturer's instructions
3. Raise the sampler slowly to avoid losing material; keep it
   horizontal as it breaks the water surface
4. Inspect the sample: a successful grab is at least half full with an
   undisturbed sediment surface and overlying water. Reject and re-
   sample if the grab is less than one-third full, tilted, or shows
   evidence of washout [@usepa2001sediment].
5. Carefully drain overlying water without disturbing the sediment
   surface
6. For surficial samples, subsample the top 2--5 cm using a stainless
   steel spoon
7. Homogenize and containerize as in Section 6.2

### Intact Cores (Hand Corer)

1. Push the acrylic core tube vertically into soft sediment to the
   desired depth (typically 10--30 cm)
2. Cap the top of the tube (creating suction) before pulling the core
   from the sediment
3. Once extracted, cap the bottom immediately
4. Label the core tube with sample ID, date, depth, and orientation
   (top/bottom)
5. Keep the core vertical during transport and store at 4 C

### Decontamination Between Sites

1. Scrub all stainless steel equipment with a brush and rinse with
   site water
2. Follow with a deionized water rinse
3. For trace metal work, perform an additional acid rinse (10% HNO~3~)
   followed by a triple DI water rinse
4. See [SOP-F007 Field Decontamination](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd)


## Sample Containers and Preservation

| Analyte                    | Container                | Preservative                |
|:---------------------------|:-------------------------|:----------------------------|
| Grain size / texture       | Whirl-Pak or poly bag    | Refrigerate 4 C             |
| Organic matter (LOI)       | Whirl-Pak or poly bag    | Refrigerate 4 C             |
| Total metals               | Glass jar (acid-washed)  | Refrigerate 4 C; freeze if holding > 7 days |
| Nutrients (N, P)           | Whirl-Pak or poly bag    | Refrigerate 4 C; freeze if holding > 48 hours |
| Organic contaminants       | Glass jar (solvent-rinsed) | Refrigerate 4 C           |
| Benthic macroinvertebrates | Separate container       | 95% ethanol or 10% formalin |

::: {.callout-note}
Confirm specific container requirements and holding times with the
analytical laboratory before each sampling event.
:::


## Quality Control

- Collect field duplicates at a rate of at least 1 per 10 samples (or
  1 per sampling event, whichever is greater)
- Collect one equipment blank per sampling event: rinse
  decontaminated equipment with DI water and submit the rinse as a
  sample
- Record all deviations from this SOP in the field notebook
- Complete the chain of custody form per
  [SOP-F008](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd)
- Photograph each grab or core before subsampling


## Data Management

1. Enter field data into the project database within 48 hours
2. Archive original field data sheets (scan if paper)
3. When laboratory results are received, merge with field data and
   apply QC flags per
   [SOP-L802](../lab_sops/SOP-L802-quality-control.qmd)

## Training Record

Before collecting sediment samples independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd), and
   [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd) in full
2. Observe a trained operator demonstrate grab sampler deployment,
   core collection, and decontamination
3. Practice deploying the Ponar or Ekman sampler (or hand corer) under
   supervision
4. Demonstrate proper homogenization, containerization, and labeling
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
